examples.problem_statement: Problem 6. Express the following in engineering notation and in prefix form: (a) 300000 W (b) 0.000068 H

solution.description: Recall what engineering notation demands before converting anything: the number is written as a coefficient multiplied by a power of ten whose index is a multiple of three, with the coefficient kept below 1000 so that a standard prefix can replace the power of ten.

solution.operation: Part (a): Convert 300000 W to engineering notation
solution.description: Shift the decimal point three places to the left in 300000 so the coefficient becomes 300, and record those three places as a factor of 10 to the third. The index 3 is a multiple of three, so this is valid engineering notation.
Look up 10 to the third in the table of prefixes: it is kilo, written k.

solution.operation: Part (a): Write final answer with prefix
solution.description: Attach that prefix to the unit, so 300 multiplied by 10 to the third watts is written 300 kW.

solution.operation: Part (b): Convert 0.000068 H to engineering notation
solution.description: For the small number 0.000068, move the decimal point six places to the right so the coefficient becomes 68, and record those six places as 10 to the power minus 6. Six is a multiple of three, so the requirement is met.
Look up 10 to the power minus 6 in the same table: it is micro, written with the Greek letter mu.

solution.operation: Part (b): Write final answer with prefix
solution.description: Attach the micro prefix to the henry, so 68 multiplied by 10 to the power minus 6 H is written 68 microhenrys.
Check both answers by converting back to ordinary decimal form: 300 kW returns 300000 W and 68 microhenrys returns 0.000068 H, matching the two values given in the question.

examples.problem_statement:
(i) $x$ into $x^3$ goes $x^2$. Put $x^2$ above $x^3$.
(ii) $x^2(x + y) = x^3 + x^2y$
(iii) Subtract.
(iv) $x$ into $-x^2y$ goes $-xy$. Put $-xy$ above the dividend.
(v) $-xy(x + y) = -x^2y - xy^2$
(vi) Subtract.
(vii) $x$ into $xy^2$ goes $y^2$. Put $y^2$ above the dividend.
(viii) $y^2(x + y) = xy^2 + y^3$
(ix) Subtract.
Thus, $\frac{x^3 + y^3}{x + y} = x^2 - xy + y^2$.
